reasons: The promql multiplies by the constant 100, which is not in the Datadog source. Datadog system.io.util is a percent, while system.disk.io_time is seconds, so the rate is a 0-1 ratio. The scale belongs in notes (unit differs: s vs %, see the OpenTelemetry system.disk.io_time definition) and must not be applied in promql.
The range is the fixed window [5m]. Only $__rate_interval is allowed as a range, so this must be rate({otel_metric_name="system.disk.io_time", otel_metric_type="sum"}[$__rate_interval]).

Quantity (fraction of time the disk is busy), aggregation (avg across series, no by-clause) and series selection (no scope matcher, since $scope has no prefix and default *) match the Datadog request. The rate() on a monotonic sum is valid.
Outcome translated is appropriate because an exact translation exists once the scale is handled in notes; the defect is in the promql text itself.
